name: Ahrefs
access_notes: API keys are created by workspace owners or admins on eligible paid plans; other plans get limited free test queries. Not enterprise-only: Ahrefs Connect apps reach Lite, Standard, Advanced and Enterprise. Ahrefs Connect needs an application and review before going live. Paid requests cost at least 50 API units.

name: Aircall
access_notes: Single-account use: any Aircall account admin can self-generate API keys (requires an existing Aircall account; plan/cost not stated). Multi-customer OAuth needs Technology Partner approval (~5 business days) before client credentials are issued.

name: Airtable
access_notes: Web API is available on all plan types with call limits: Free 1000 calls per workspace per month, Team 100,000, Business and Enterprise unlimited. Organization admins may need to allowlist a token for organization-owned bases.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
access_notes: Developers register in the Solution Provider Portal and must request and qualify for roles. Restricted roles that expose PII need enhanced security. Public apps need Amazon approval to publish to the Selling Partner Appstore. Cost is not stated on the fetched pages.

name: Apify
access_notes: Create a free Console account, then a personal API token on the Integrations page; the token is shown only once. Paid plans and pricing are not on the fetched pages.

name: Asana
access_notes: PATs generated in developer console; API rate limits published for both Free and Paid domains, so API works on free plans. Service accounts are Enterprise-only.

name: Attio
access_notes: Free plan is $0 for up to 3 users; every new workspace gets a 14-day Pro trial. Pricing FAQ says every plan includes the MCP server. Workspace admin must authorize workspace-level tokens, which is ordinary install consent rather than an approval gate. Some features (custom objects, call intelligence) are Pro and above.

name: BigCommerce
access_notes: Free BigCommerce trial store available for testing. Merchants create store-level API credentials in Settings > Store-level API accounts; app-level credentials are created in the Developer Portal. Cost of a production store and any plan gate are not stated.

name: Binance
access_notes: API keys are created in the Binance account; a Binance account is required. Official key-creation and regional/KYC rules not verified because the help page and developer portal returned no text. Binance.US is a separate entity with its own API.

name: Brex
access_notes: Own account: account or card admin accepts the developer API agreement and creates a token. Third-party multi-tenant OAuth is partner-only.

name: Bright Data
access_notes: Self-serve signup with free tier of 5,000 credits/month, no card. API key is created in account settings by an admin. Scraper API pay-as-you-go $1.50 per 1,000 records as of Sept 2026; Scale plan $1.30 per 1,000 beyond included volume. Agent registration via emailed code also documented.

name: Clay
access_notes: Pricing page lists Clay API access under the Enterprise plan (custom pricing, annual commitment); Growth lists HTTP API integrations (outbound) and webhooks. Developer docs do not state a plan gate; key creation is self-serve in the app. Gating of the Public API is ambiguous.

name: ClickUp
access_notes: Rate limits apply to FreeForever plan (100/min), so API is available on free plans; Enterprise gets 10,000/min and user management API.

name: Close
access_notes: API keys are generated under Settings > Developer > API Keys. Keys follow the owner's access. Cost and plan requirements are not stated on the fetched pages. Non-Close users must email support@close.com for a free Dev organization.

name: Cloudflare
access_notes: API tokens created in dashboard on a free account; OAuth client creation needs admin-type role plus DNS verification for public clients. Client API limit 1200 req/5 min per token; some endpoints plan-gated by product.

name: Coda
access_notes: Free of charge for all users in free and paid workspaces. Actions depend on the token owner's workspace role; createDoc requires a Doc Maker or Admin role.

name: Consensus
access_notes: REST Search API is optional on Team and Enterprise plans 'available upon approval, rate limited' with pricing via consensus.app/home/api; Enterprise custom. MCP server with OAuth works with a free account (limited quotas).

name: Copper
access_notes: API keys are generated in System settings > API Keys (self-serve). The API is available on trial, professional and business plans. OAuth requires contacting Copper to register the app. No prices on the fetched pages.

name: Datadog
access_notes: Credentials are created in the customer's Datadog org; a free trial exists but pricing is paid per product. No self-serve free tier shown on fetched pages. Rate limits raised via support. [sandbox_or_test_env: Free Datadog trial account (duration not verified on fetched pages)] [api_surface.webhooks: outbound webhooks integration (Datadog calls your URL from monitor alerts)] [api_surface.rate_limits_documented: yes]

name: DataForSEO
access_notes: Free account gives credentials and free Sandbox; real calls draw on prepaid balance, pay-as-you-go with $50 minimum top-up, no subscriptions.

name: DealCloud
access_notes: The API must be enabled for the user's group by a site admin (Admin > User Management). Customers without the Admin section go through their admin or DealCloud CSM. API pricing is not stated. MCP requires the Celeste license.

name: Devin
access_notes: Self-serve service user provisioning for Teams/standard orgs; Devin Cloud (which the API drives) is listed from the Pro plan ($20/mo) up, not the Free plan. Enterprise API scope (cross-org analytics, audit) is for enterprise customers. Plan-by-plan API gating not fully legible in the fetched pricing table.

name: Discord
access_notes: Credentials are self-serve: a bot user is created in the Developer Portal and generates a bot token. Some OAuth2 scopes need approval from Discord. Cost is not stated on the fetched pages.

name: Ecwid
access_notes: Only stores on paid plans can access the API; free upgrade for test stores on request to API support. Public App Market apps go through validation. [sandbox_or_test_env: No test mode in the API; docs recommend a separate test store (free paid-plan upgrade on request).]

name: fanbasis
access_notes: Official Checkout API exists (npm SDK, sandbox env); docs not readable.

name: Fathom
access_notes: Generate an API key in User Settings → API Access. The FAQ says API access (keys and webhooks) is included on all plans. API keys are per user; there are no org-level keys.

name: Firecrawl
access_notes: Free plan: 1,000 credits/month, no card required, self-serve key. Paid: Hobby $19/mo monthly or $16/mo annual; Standard $99/$83; Growth $399/$333; Scale $749/$599. No wait or approval stated.

name: Freshdesk
access_notes: API key is available to any agent in any account incl. trials (trial default limit 50 calls/min). Rate limit is plan based: Growth 100, Pro 400, Enterprise 700 per minute. No plan is stated to lack API access.

name: Front
access_notes: Free 14-day trial with all Professional features, no credit card. Rate limit 50/100/200 rpm by plan (Starter/Pro/Enterprise); increases need Professional+. Partner integrations get a separate 120 rpm.

name: GitHub
access_notes: Third-party listing: free with rate limits; GitHub subscription not required for API access. Official pricing page not in the pages.

name: Gladly
access_notes: Requires a Gladly customer account; an administrator grants API User permission, then user creates API token. Sandbox at {organization}.gladly.qa.

name: GoHighLevel
access_notes: API access is included in Starter ($97/month), Unlimited ($297/month) and Founder ($497/month) plans. PITs are created in Settings with no review stated. Some endpoints, such as Create Sub-Account, need the Founder plan.

name: Google Ads
access_notes: Enabling the API gives Test access automatically. Production access requires applying for Explorer (2,880 ops/day), Basic (15,000 ops/day) or Standard (unlimited) access; Standard needs a manual compliance audit, typically about 10 business days. Cost is not stated in the cached pages.

name: Gorgias
access_notes: Pricing page: 'Start free trial No credit card required'; API rate limit 2 req/s listed on every plan. Distributable OAuth apps need partner-portal registration and tech partnership review; developer sandbox requires emailing techpartners.

name: Grain
access_notes: Personal Access Token is generated in Account settings, Integrations, Personal API, and is available on every plan including Free. Workspace tokens need a workspace admin on Business or Enterprise.

name: Gumroad
access_notes: Applications and access tokens are created in any seller account's settings; no approval step or plan gate found. Gumroad charges per-sale fees, not API fees.

name: Harvest
access_notes: Tokens and OAuth apps are created self-serve in Harvest ID. Harvest account needed; pricing page says free trial, no credit card, and the free plan is 1 seat. No plan gating of API found on the pricing page.

name: Help Scout
access_notes: Help Scout support article: 'The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations.' Standard 200 calls/min without reporting endpoints; Plus 400; Pro 800. Standard and Plus offer a free trial.

name: higgsfield
access_notes: Self-serve: account, payment method, top up USD balance (min $5), create key.

name: HubSpot
access_notes: Standard HubSpot accounts can be free; developer test accounts are free (up to 10). Private-distribution OAuth apps are limited to 10 accounts; Marketplace listing is manually reviewed and needs 3 active installs, but is not required to call the API. Some scopes are tiered by plan; rate limits depend on account subscription.

name: Intercom
access_notes: Private apps for your own paid workspace need no review. Public multi-customer apps must be reviewed and approved by Intercom. Free development workspaces exist.

name: iPayX
access_notes: llms.txt lists API plans from $99/mo; MCP has free tools and 3 free audits per IP per month; key via ipayx.ai/ai-access (JS shell, not read).

name: Jira
access_notes: Jira has a Free pricing tier; API tokens and 3LO apps are self-serve. Plan-level API gating not found. Rate limits are points-based per hour, enforced from 2 Mar 2026.

name: Klaviyo
access_notes: A free plan exists. Creating a private key needs an Owner, Admin or Manager role. A linked test account can be created (starts on the free plan). Marketplace listing requires OAuth. [sandbox_or_test_env: test account: a regular Klaviyo account with a test label, starts on free plan, same production environment]

name: Lark (Larksuite)
access_notes: Custom apps created self-serve in the Developer Console; each API scope needs enterprise administrator approval before calls work. Store apps limited to ISV-qualified users. Pricing/plan gating of API not found (plans page returned no text).

name: Linear
access_notes: API and webhook access is included on every plan including Free (pricing table). Rate limits: API key 2,500/hr, OAuth app 5,000/hr.

name: LinkedIn Ads
access_notes: Advertising API is a vetted product with Development and Standard tiers, applied for via the increasing-access link. Every app starts at Development; Standard requires a support ticket. Ad accounts must be Enterprise or Business. No price is stated in the cached pages.

name: LiveAgent
access_notes: Admin generates the v3 API key under Configuration > System > API, which is self-serve. Pages mention a free trial account for testing but do not state which plans include API access or any cost.

name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
access_notes: No central developer signup: the store admin creates an integration or admin token on each instance. Magento Open Source is free (OSL 3.0); Adobe Commerce is licensed/paid. SaaS needs Adobe IMS project credentials.

name: Mailchimp
access_notes: API key and OAuth app registration are self-serve in a Mailchimp account; a Free plan exists. Whether specific features are plan-limited was not verified.

name: Mermaid CLI
access_notes: Open-source package installed locally with npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli. No account, key or cost stated for the CLI.

name: Meta Ads
access_notes: Own ad accounts: standard access to ads_read/ads_management works without review. Managing other businesses' accounts needs advanced access via per-permission App Review and business verification. Marketing API tier Limited (default) vs Full (500 successful calls in 15 days, under 15% errors). Free per call. Evidence is third-party summaries of Meta docs.

name: Monday.com
access_notes: API is a free feature across all plans (daily call limit 200 on Free); viewers, guests (no key), student accounts cannot get tokens. Free developer account available for testing.

name: MongoDB Atlas
access_notes: Any Atlas account holder who is Organization Owner can create service accounts or API keys; no sales or approval step is stated. Free M0 tier exists. Whether Admin API works on M0 not separately verified. [sandbox_or_test_env: Free forever M0 cluster tier] [oauth_details.app_review_required: no (service accounts self-created by Org Owner)]

name: MrScraper
access_notes: Free API token from mrscraper.com per the vendor blog, which describes a free tier. Free-tier limits and paid pricing are not verified from the fetched pages, and some blog text is truncated.

name: Neo4j
access_notes: Created in Aura console under Account Settings > Client credentials; all tiers can create credentials; no cost or wait stated. Client secret is shown only once.

name: Netlify
access_notes: Tokens and OAuth apps are self-serve in user settings; a Free plan is offered. Rate limit 500 req/min for most requests, deploys 3/min and 100/day.

name: NotebookLM
access_notes: Personal API: enable notebook.googleapis.com in own Cloud project, OAuth with personal Google account that signed in to Gemini Notebook once; no paid plan stated in prerequisites. Enterprise API requires Gemini Notebook Enterprise licenses. Public Preview, pricing/quota of personal API not stated.

name: Notion
access_notes: Quickstart needs only a Notion account and a PAT from the Developer portal; no plan tier required. Business/Enterprise admins may restrict PAT creation. [sandbox_or_test_env: Use a free personal workspace (no dedicated sandbox documented)]

name: Otter AI
access_notes: Public API reportedly available to Enterprise workspaces only (Enterprise is contact sales). Official pricing lists the Otter MCP server as a feature of the free Basic plan. Official help articles were not fetchable.

name: Paygent Connect
access_notes: No Paygent Connect sign-up, credential or pricing pages were found. The paygent.to pages mention a free beta, which belongs to a different product.

name: Pinterest
access_notes: Create a developer account, describe your app, and submit it for review. The pages do not state review turnaround or cost.

name: Pipedrive
access_notes: Requires a Pipedrive company account (ZoomInfo review says API access on all paid plans incl. Lite $14/seat; trial not verified). Free developer sandbox account available via request form (5 seats; deleted if inactive). Developers in sanctioned countries are excluded. Token-based daily budget: 30,000 x plan multiplier x seats.

name: PitchBook
access_notes: Third-party guide: API/Direct Data priced by quote, separate from platform; no public key signup. Official pages unreadable (403).

name: Plaid
access_notes: Sandbox free via Dashboard signup; Production requires application and approval.

name: Plain
access_notes: Pricing page: 'Start today, no credit card required.' Paid plans Foundation $45-55 and Horizon $99 per user/month billed annually; no plan gate on API or machine users stated.

name: Podio
access_notes: Free plan (up to 5 users) lists 1000 API calls per hour; higher limits need paid API add-ons (paid plans only). Some operations need Podio support approval per first pass.

name: Pumble
access_notes: Pricing page states the FREE plan has no limitations; no plan gate for API addon or app creation is stated. Needs a user able to install the addon in the workspace. 7-day trial of paid features also offered.

name: Pylon
access_notes: Pricing page lists REST API, MCP and Webhooks under the Professional seat ($89/seat, annual contract). Free trials are arranged through a sales rep; no self-serve signup seen.

name: QuickBooks
access_notes: Free Builder partner tier ($0, 500,000 CorePlus credits/month, blocked after); Silver $300, Gold $1,700, Platinum $4,500; premium APIs need Silver+ and a support ticket. Go-live app review not verified from fetched pages.

name: Ramp
access_notes: Create a developer app as a business admin, with client credentials and scopes, for your own business. Sandbox is requested through an access form and is ready in about one minute. Publishing for other businesses needs a partner application and a production access application. Cost is not stated in the fetched pages.

name: Reducto
access_notes: Standard pay-as-you-go plan with $150 free usage then list rates; Growth/Enterprise via sales add rate limits, BAA, data residency. Startup program credits.

name: Salesforce
access_notes: API access included in Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance and Developer (free dev org); Professional needs a paid API add-on; Essentials has none (third-party guide citing Salesforce Help, read 2026-11-19). Commercial multi-tenant apps are said to need AppExchange Partner Program enrolment under updated API terms (Sliick, third party).

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
access_notes: Official docs unreadable (HTTP 403). The third-party repo requires a Commerce Cloud instance with OCAPI access and credentials; how those are obtained, cost, and wait are not stated.

name: SE Ranking
access_notes: Key is generated in the API Dashboard. Data API calls draw on credits included with paid plans or bought as pay-as-you-go packs. Project API uses subscription limits on every current plan. Practically, API access needs a paid subscription or PAYG purchase.

name: SendGrid
access_notes: Free plan retired from May 27, 2025: sending paused on free plans after 60 days. New accounts get a free trial, no credit card; paid plans required afterwards (Essentials about $19.95/mo per third-party search summary).

name: Sentry
access_notes: Internal integrations and tokens are self-created under Settings > Developer Settings. Free Developer plan ($0) exists; pricing page lists 'API & third-party integrations' under the Team plan, so free-plan API limits are unverified. [sandbox_or_test_env: Free Developer plan ($0, one user) usable as a test org]

name: Sherlock
access_notes: No hosted API and no account or key for the CLI.

name: Shopify
access_notes: Dev Dashboard and free dev stores are self-serve for building. Some scopes need Shopify's approval and public apps need protected-customer-data approval; App Store listing is reviewed. Whether a Partner account costs anything is not stated on fetched pages.

name: Slack
access_notes: Create an app and install to a workspace self-serve; Web API rate tiers are identical across plans. Commercial distribution of apps must go through the Slack Marketplace (review); non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps get conversations.history/replies at 1 req/min, 15 objects. Internal custom apps keep 50+/min, 1000 objects.

name: Smartsheet
access_notes: API and MCP require Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan. OAuth Developer Tools registration requires Smartsheet to accept a request; denial is escalated via Customer Success Manager.

name: Snowflake
access_notes: No vendor app review; credentials are issued inside each customer's own account. Free 30-day trial needs only an email; trial ends at 30 days or credit depletion, then suspended. [sandbox_or_test_env: 30-day free trial account (no payment info); AI features disabled until credit card added] [api_surface.pagination_documented: yes (result partitions)] [oauth_details.app_review_required: no]

name: Squarespace
access_notes: API keys need a Commerce Advanced plan site. OAuth client registration is reviewed by Squarespace before client_id/secret are issued; Extensions listing is a separate process.

name: Stripe
access_notes: Keys are generated on account creation; sandbox keys work immediately. Live-mode money movement requires account activation (business verification). No per-call fee for API access.

name: Supabase
access_notes: PATs generated in account page; OAuth apps self-serve via building an integration. Free plan exists (2 active projects, paused after 1 week inactivity). Management API rate limited.

name: systeme.io
access_notes: Keys are generated by the account holder under Settings > MCP & API keys. A free plan exists (no credit card). No page states that API access is restricted to paid plans; the pricing page lists an 'API requests per minute' row but values were not extracted, so per-plan rate limits are unverified.

name: Telegram
access_notes: Overview page says both the Bot API and the client API are free of charge. Bot accounts need no extra phone number. Gateway API is paid at $0.01 per delivered code, with free testing.

name: Threads (Meta)
access_notes: Free. A Meta app plus your own Threads account as a tester works the same day for your own account. Accessing other people's accounts in production needs Meta's App Review.

name: Twenty
access_notes: Cloud: 30-day trial, no credit card; Pro $9/user/mo includes REST & GraphQL API, webhooks, MCP. Self-hosting the open-source core is free. API is not plan-gated, only rate limited (50/min Pro, 100/min Organization, custom Enterprise).

name: Twilio
access_notes: Free trial without credit card: 100 SMS, 75 voice minutes etc, expires after 30 days; trial messaging limited to verified numbers. Production is pay-as-you-go (US SMS $0.0083/segment); US A2P 10DLC registration requires a paid account.

name: Vercel
access_notes: Access tokens are self-serve; a free Hobby plan exists. Some features are plan-gated (account webhooks are Pro/Enterprise). Rate limits apply per action.

name: Vonage
access_notes: Sign up at dashboard.vonage.com to get API key and secret immediately; free credit on signup, then pay-per-request. US A2P SMS needs 10DLC registration.

name: Waterfall.io
access_notes: Keys are not self-serve: docs say to contact the team for API access and pricing. No public rate card; pricing is quoted after a benchmark on your data. No free trial stated.

name: WhatsApp Business
access_notes: Free API access, per-message billing. Needs a Meta developer app, business portfolio, phone number, approved display name; business verification to raise limits. Test number available. Third-party sources only.

name: WooCommerce
access_notes: Store admin generates Consumer Key and Consumer Secret in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API; the core plugin is described as free. Consumer Secret is shown only once. Legacy REST API needs a separate free plugin.

name: Xero
access_notes: Starter plan: max 5 connections, no payment method, 1000 calls/day/org. Plus and above need App Certification; Advanced/Enterprise need security assessment. Journals, XPM, bulk connections gated.

name: YouTube Transcript
access_notes: Free signup with 100 credits and no card required. Paid plans start at $5/month for 1,000 credits, with top-ups at $2.50 per 1K. One credit per successful request.

name: Zendesk
access_notes: Pricing page lists only paid per-agent plans (Support Team from US$19/agent/month). Trial and sandbox not verified. Rate limits vary by plan (200 to 2500 req/min).

name: Zoho Cliq
access_notes: A Free Cliq plan exists (pricing page; paid Standard US$18/month up to 25 users, Professional US$2/user/month, Enterprise US$4/user/month). Apps are registered self-serve in the Zoho API console. No documented API plan gating found; unverified.

name: Zoho CRM
access_notes: Developer Console registration is open; API credit table includes a Free Edition (5000 credits/24h) and trial editions share paid-edition limits. Higher tiers get more credits. Per-region data center handling required.
